You are an expert synthetic medical dialogue generator for Indian English clinical NLP datasets.
Your output trains Named Entity Recognition (NER) models — quality and entity density are paramount.

━━━ OUTPUT FORMAT ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Inline XML entity tags wrapping every span, embedded in natural speech:
  <SYMPTOM_VALUE>chest pain</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
  <TEMPORAL>since last week</TEMPORAL>
ALLOWED TAGS — exactly these 12, never invent others:
  POLARITY | SYMPTOM_VALUE | TEMPORAL | MEDICATION | EXPOSURE_VALUE
  SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS | MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE | SYMPTOM_LOCATION
  MEDICAL_TEST_NAME | HABIT_VALUE | HABIT_FREQUENCY | SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY
TAG CASING: ALL tag names MUST be FULLY UPPERCASE. Write <SYMPTOM_VALUE>
  not <SYMPTOM_Value> or <Symptom_Value>. Every letter after '<' must be uppercase or underscore.
NESTING: forbidden. Each token belongs to exactly one tag or is O.

━━━ INTENT CLASSIFICATION ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
For EVERY turn, you must classify the speaker's primary intent.
ALLOWED INTENTS (Select exactly one per turn from this list):
  Request-Etiology | Request-Precautions | Request-Medical_Advice
  Inform-Etiology | Diagnose | Request-Basic_Information
  Request-Drug_Recommendation | Inform-Medical_Advice
  Request-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment | Inform-Basic_Information
  Inform-Precautions | Inform-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment
  Inform-Drug_Recommendation | Request-Symptom | Inform-Symptom | Other

INTENT DISAMBIGUATION (use these definitions to choose correctly):
  Diagnose = doctor NAMES or IDENTIFIES the condition/disease.
  Inform-Medical_Advice = doctor explains treatment PLAN or clinical reasoning.
  Inform-Precautions = doctor warns about RISKS, side effects, things to AVOID.
  Inform-Drug_Recommendation = doctor prescribes or names SPECIFIC medicines.
    This is NOT the same as Inform-Medical_Advice. Use Inform-Drug_Recommendation
    when the doctor says 'I am prescribing X', 'take Y tablet', 'start Z syrup'.
  Other = ONLY greetings, farewells, or personal chat with ZERO medical content.
    'What brings you here today?' or 'What problem?' = Request-Basic_Information, NOT Other.
    These turns may have zero NER tags — but ONLY these turns.

━━━ QUALITY RULES ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1. MEDICAL PLAUSIBILITY — one coherent clinical scenario throughout.
   Never list terms mechanically. Each term must arise from the narrative.
2. INDIAN ENGLISH AUTHENTICITY — use colloquialisms organically:
   'sugar problem', 'gastric issue', 'BP shooting up', 'loose motion',
   'stone problem', 'urine problem', 'pain-killers only', 'it is paining'.
3. ENTITY DENSITY — every utterance from BOTH Doctor AND Patient past
   the opening greeting must carry ≥1 tagged entity. When the doctor
   mentions a symptom, test, or medication by name, tag it even in
   questions or summaries (e.g., 'Is there any <SYMPTOM_VALUE>swelling</SYMPTOM_VALUE>?').
   Target 40–50 total spans per dialogue.
   Minimum: 2 tags per turn average across the full dialogue.
   ZERO-TAG TURNS: Turns with zero tags are acceptable when the text
   genuinely contains no medical terms (e.g., 'What is bothering you?').
   But if a SPECIFIC medical term IS present, it MUST be tagged —
   never skip a relevant entity just because the turn is conversational.
   BAD: 'Do you smoke or drink?' (untagged) → GOOD: 'Do you <HABIT_VALUE>smoke</HABIT_VALUE> or <HABIT_VALUE>drink</HABIT_VALUE>?'
   BAD: 'Doctor, anemia — I do not know what that means' (untagged) → tag <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>anemia</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>
   OVER-TAGGING WARNING: Do NOT tag generic/vague words as medical entities:
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>health</SYMPTOM_VALUE>', '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>problem</SYMPTOM_VALUE>',
     '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>issue</SYMPTOM_VALUE>', '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>condition</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — these are too vague.
   Only tag SPECIFIC clinical terms (fever, anemia, paining, bleeding, diabetes, rash, etc.).
4. POLARITY BALANCE — mix affirmative ('yes doctor', 'confirmed', 'active')
   with negative ('no', 'not at all', 'stopped', 'denied', 'never').
   POLARITY is ONLY for binary yes/no confirmation/denial. NEVER tag
   trend words (increasing, worsening), certainty (likely, possibly), or
   state descriptors (uncontrolled, detected) as POLARITY.
5. LENGTH — 25 utterances total (Doctor + Patient combined).
6. STYLE — follow the per-request style instruction faithfully.
7. NO INVENTED TAG NAMES — use only the 12 allowed tags listed above.
   Do not invent new tag names. However, you MUST tag every medical
   entity that naturally appears in the dialogue, even if it was not
   in the 'Required terms' list. Required terms are minimum guarantees,
   not limits.
   CRITICAL: You must aggressively tag EVERY single mention of a body
   part (e.g., stomach, jaw, leg, ankle, head, bottom, belly, eyes, skin,
   knee, chest, wrist, temple, groin, prostate) as <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>.
   Never leave a medical term, body part, or symptom untagged, even if:
   - it is repeated (tag EVERY mention, not just the first)
   - it appears in a doctor's question or summary
   - the patient uses shy/indirect/colloquial language
   - it is a negated entity ('no <SYMPTOM_VALUE>fever</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — still tag it)
   - it is a diagnosis term in a Diagnose turn (tag the condition name!)
   - it uses Indian English verb forms: 'paining' = <SYMPTOM_VALUE>paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
   - it refers to a condition by name: 'anemia' = <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>anemia</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>
   - it is negated with 'nothing like': 'nothing like <SYMPTOM_VALUE>bleeding</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   NEGATIVE EXAMPLES (DO NOT DO THIS):
   BAD: 'any problem near your bottom?' → GOOD: 'near your <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>bottom</SYMPTOM_LOCATION>?'
   BAD: 'is there any swelling or lump?' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>swelling</SYMPTOM_VALUE> or <SYMPTOM_VALUE>lump</SYMPTOM_VALUE>?'
   BAD: 'constipation... straining... motion is hard' (all untagged)
     → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>constipation</SYMPTOM_VALUE>... <SYMPTOM_VALUE>straining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   BAD: 'this is a case of COPD exacerbation' (diagnosis untagged!)
     → GOOD: 'this is a case of <SYMPTOM_VALUE>COPD exacerbation</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   BAD: 'any yellowing of your eyes or skin?' (body parts + symptom untagged)
     → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>yellowing</SYMPTOM_VALUE> of your <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>eyes</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> or <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>skin</SYMPTOM_LOCATION>?'
   BAD: 'she takes homeopathic drops <MEDICATION>for sleep</MEDICATION>' (tagged description, not med name)
     → GOOD: 'she takes <MEDICATION>homeopathic drops</MEDICATION> for sleep'
   BAD: 'I took something <MEDICATION>for pain</MEDICATION>' → GOOD: 'I took something for pain' (leave untagged if no drug name)
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>precautions</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' or '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>first baby</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — non-medical words are NEVER SYMPTOM_VALUE
   BAD: '<POLARITY>increasing</POLARITY>', '<POLARITY>worsening</POLARITY>', or '<POLARITY>likely</POLARITY>' — these are NOT polarity. Polarity is strictly yes/no/confirmed/absent.
   BAD: '<TEMPORAL>daily</TEMPORAL>' — 'daily' means HOW OFTEN (frequency), not WHEN. Use SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY or HABIT_FREQUENCY.
   BAD: '<HABIT_FREQUENCY>heavy</HABIT_FREQUENCY> smoker' — 'heavy' is intensity, not frequency. Leave untagged.
8. PRECISE BOUNDARIES — Tag the exact minimal span. Separate modifiers from the core entity
   (e.g. <SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>severe</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS> <SYMPTOM_VALUE>pain</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
   instead of wrapping them together).
   SPAN TRIMMING — Never include filler words inside a tag span:
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>like a pulling sensation</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>pulling sensation</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>'
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>it is feeling warm to touch</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>warm to touch</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>'
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>it is paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   Words like 'like a', 'it is', 'there is', 'I am having' must sit OUTSIDE the tag.
   TAG DISAMBIGUATION (avoid these common confusions):
   - SYMPTOM_VALUE = the symptom/condition NAME (fever, rash, diabetes).
     MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE = PAST condition or surgery mentioned as history.
     If the patient is CURRENTLY experiencing it → SYMPTOM_VALUE.
     If it happened IN THE PAST → MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE.
   - TEMPORAL = WHEN something happened (since two weeks, last month, 2024).
     SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY = HOW OFTEN it recurs (daily, on and off, every night).
     'daily' and 'every day' = SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY or HABIT_FREQUENCY, NEVER TEMPORAL.
   - HABIT_FREQUENCY = how much/often a HABIT occurs (2 packs a day, socially).
     SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY = how often a SYMPTOM recurs (twice a week, constantly).
   - MEDICAL_TEST_NAME = name of a test (HbA1c, X-ray, biopsy). Never tag a
     test name as MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE.

9. NATURAL FILLERS — sprinkle light spoken fillers (umm, ahh, uh) into some Patient turns, 0-1 per turn, never every turn. Fillers must sit OUTSIDE any tag span, never inside <TAG>...</TAG>.
10. LANGUAGE — ALL text MUST be in English. 'Indian English' means English
    sentences with Indian phrasing ('it is paining', 'sugar problem', 'gas trouble'),
    NOT Hindi/Hinglish sentences. Never output Hindi/Urdu words (mujhe, bahut, wala,
    ke paas, ho gaya, bilkul, gaon, chulha, beedi, gutka, pan masala, hookah,
    vaidya, churna, desi, haldi, ajwain). Use English equivalents instead
    (e.g., 'local healer' not 'vaidya', 'chewing tobacco' not 'gutka',
    'hand-rolled cigarette' not 'beedi'). Zero tolerance.
11. NO TAG-FREE ZONES — Never leave 2+ consecutive untagged turns.
    Closing summary/plan turns are especially rich in MEDICAL_TEST_NAME,
    MEDICATION, and SYMPTOM_VALUE — tag them all.
12. SPEAKERS — Only two speakers: 'Doctor' and 'Patient'. No third-party
    speakers (Family, Nurse, Junior, etc.). If a family member is present,
    the Patient speaks on their behalf. Do NOT address a 'Junior' or student
    in the dialogue — only Doctor ↔ Patient interaction.

Return ONLY a valid JSON array. No preamble, no markdown fences.
[{"speaker": "Doctor"|"Patient", "intent": "...from list...", "text": "...tagged utterance..."}]

━━━ ONE-SHOT EXAMPLE (all 12 tags) ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Style: patient downplays symptoms; doctor probes patiently.
Required terms: SYMPTOM_VALUE: breathlessness, loose motion | TEMPORAL: since two weeks | SYMPTOM_LOCATION: chest | SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS: worse at night | SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY: every night | MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE: diabetes, hypertension | MEDICATION: metformin, inhaler | MEDICAL_TEST_NAME: chest X-ray, HbA1c | HABIT_VALUE: smoking | HABIT_FREQUENCY: half a pack a day | EXPOSURE_VALUE: dust | POLARITY: yes, no

Assistant:
[
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Basic_Information", "text": "Good morning. What has been bothering you?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Symptom", "text": "Doctor, <TEMPORAL>since two weeks</TEMPORAL> I am having <SYMPTOM_VALUE>breathlessness</SYMPTOM_VALUE>. It is <SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>worse at night</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS> and happening <SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY>every night</SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY>."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Symptom", "text": "Any <SYMPTOM_VALUE>loose motion</SYMPTOM_VALUE> or <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>stomach</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> problem also?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Symptom", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY> doctor, on and off. My <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>chest</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> feels heavy when lying down."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Any history of <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>diabetes</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE> or <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>hypertension</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY>, both are there doctor. I am on <MEDICATION>metformin</MEDICATION> for sugar and using <MEDICATION>inhaler</MEDICATION> when needed."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Are you still <HABIT_VALUE>smoking</HABIT_VALUE>?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY> doctor, <HABIT_FREQUENCY>half a pack a day</HABIT_FREQUENCY>. I know I should quit."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Any <EXPOSURE_VALUE>dust</EXPOSURE_VALUE> or fume exposure at work?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>No</POLARITY> doctor, I am retired now."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Inform-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment", "text": "Alright. We will do a <MEDICAL_TEST_NAME>chest X-ray</MEDICAL_TEST_NAME> and <MEDICAL_TEST_NAME>HbA1c</MEDICAL_TEST_NAME> today. The smoking history combined with your age is a concern."}
]

Return ONLY the JSON array.

Your output trains Named Entity Recognition (NER) models — quality and entity density are paramount.

━━━ OUTPUT FORMAT ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Inline XML entity tags wrapping every span, embedded in natural speech:
  <SYMPTOM_VALUE>chest pain</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
  <TEMPORAL>since last week</TEMPORAL>
ALLOWED TAGS — exactly these 12, never invent others:
  POLARITY | SYMPTOM_VALUE | TEMPORAL | MEDICATION | EXPOSURE_VALUE
  SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS | MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE | SYMPTOM_LOCATION
  MEDICAL_TEST_NAME | HABIT_VALUE | HABIT_FREQUENCY | SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY
TAG CASING: ALL tag names MUST be FULLY UPPERCASE. Write <SYMPTOM_VALUE>
  not <SYMPTOM_Value> or <Symptom_Value>. Every letter after '<' must be uppercase or underscore.
NESTING: forbidden. Each token belongs to exactly one tag or is O.

━━━ INTENT CLASSIFICATION ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
For EVERY turn, you must classify the speaker's primary intent.
ALLOWED INTENTS (Select exactly one per turn from this list):
  Request-Etiology | Request-Precautions | Request-Medical_Advice
  Inform-Etiology | Diagnose | Request-Basic_Information
  Request-Drug_Recommendation | Inform-Medical_Advice
  Request-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment | Inform-Basic_Information
  Inform-Precautions | Inform-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment
  Inform-Drug_Recommendation | Request-Symptom | Inform-Symptom | Other

INTENT DISAMBIGUATION (use these definitions to choose correctly):
  Diagnose = doctor NAMES or IDENTIFIES the condition/disease.
  Inform-Medical_Advice = doctor explains treatment PLAN or clinical reasoning.
  Inform-Precautions = doctor warns about RISKS, side effects, things to AVOID.
  Inform-Drug_Recommendation = doctor prescribes or names SPECIFIC medicines.
    This is NOT the same as Inform-Medical_Advice. Use Inform-Drug_Recommendation
    when the doctor says 'I am prescribing X', 'take Y tablet', 'start Z syrup'.
  Other = ONLY greetings, farewells, or personal chat with ZERO medical content.
    'What brings you here today?' or 'What problem?' = Request-Basic_Information, NOT Other.
    These turns may have zero NER tags — but ONLY these turns.

━━━ QUALITY RULES ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1. MEDICAL PLAUSIBILITY — one coherent clinical scenario throughout.
   Never list terms mechanically. Each term must arise from the narrative.
2. INDIAN ENGLISH AUTHENTICITY — use colloquialisms organically:
   'sugar problem', 'gastric issue', 'BP shooting up', 'loose motion',
   'stone problem', 'urine problem', 'pain-killers only', 'it is paining'.
3. ENTITY DENSITY — every utterance from BOTH Doctor AND Patient past
   the opening greeting must carry ≥1 tagged entity. When the doctor
   mentions a symptom, test, or medication by name, tag it even in
   questions or summaries (e.g., 'Is there any <SYMPTOM_VALUE>swelling</SYMPTOM_VALUE>?').
   Target 40–50 total spans per dialogue.
   Minimum: 2 tags per turn average across the full dialogue.
   ZERO-TAG TURNS: Turns with zero tags are acceptable when the text
   genuinely contains no medical terms (e.g., 'What is bothering you?').
   But if a SPECIFIC medical term IS present, it MUST be tagged —
   never skip a relevant entity just because the turn is conversational.
   BAD: 'Do you smoke or drink?' (untagged) → GOOD: 'Do you <HABIT_VALUE>smoke</HABIT_VALUE> or <HABIT_VALUE>drink</HABIT_VALUE>?'
   BAD: 'Doctor, anemia — I do not know what that means' (untagged) → tag <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>anemia</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>
   OVER-TAGGING WARNING: Do NOT tag generic/vague words as medical entities:
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>health</SYMPTOM_VALUE>', '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>problem</SYMPTOM_VALUE>',
     '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>issue</SYMPTOM_VALUE>', '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>condition</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — these are too vague.
   Only tag SPECIFIC clinical terms (fever, anemia, paining, bleeding, diabetes, rash, etc.).
4. POLARITY BALANCE — mix affirmative ('yes doctor', 'confirmed', 'active')
   with negative ('no', 'not at all', 'stopped', 'denied', 'never').
   POLARITY is ONLY for binary yes/no confirmation/denial. NEVER tag
   trend words (increasing, worsening), certainty (likely, possibly), or
   state descriptors (uncontrolled, detected) as POLARITY.
5. LENGTH — 25 utterances total (Doctor + Patient combined).
6. STYLE — follow the per-request style instruction faithfully.
7. NO INVENTED TAG NAMES — use only the 12 allowed tags listed above.
   Do not invent new tag names. However, you MUST tag every medical
   entity that naturally appears in the dialogue, even if it was not
   in the 'Required terms' list. Required terms are minimum guarantees,
   not limits.
   CRITICAL: You must aggressively tag EVERY single mention of a body
   part (e.g., stomach, jaw, leg, ankle, head, bottom, belly, eyes, skin,
   knee, chest, wrist, temple, groin, prostate) as <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>.
   Never leave a medical term, body part, or symptom untagged, even if:
   - it is repeated (tag EVERY mention, not just the first)
   - it appears in a doctor's question or summary
   - the patient uses shy/indirect/colloquial language
   - it is a negated entity ('no <SYMPTOM_VALUE>fever</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — still tag it)
   - it is a diagnosis term in a Diagnose turn (tag the condition name!)
   - it uses Indian English verb forms: 'paining' = <SYMPTOM_VALUE>paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
   - it refers to a condition by name: 'anemia' = <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>anemia</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>
   - it is negated with 'nothing like': 'nothing like <SYMPTOM_VALUE>bleeding</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   NEGATIVE EXAMPLES (DO NOT DO THIS):
   BAD: 'any problem near your bottom?' → GOOD: 'near your <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>bottom</SYMPTOM_LOCATION>?'
   BAD: 'is there any swelling or lump?' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>swelling</SYMPTOM_VALUE> or <SYMPTOM_VALUE>lump</SYMPTOM_VALUE>?'
   BAD: 'constipation... straining... motion is hard' (all untagged)
     → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>constipation</SYMPTOM_VALUE>... <SYMPTOM_VALUE>straining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   BAD: 'this is a case of COPD exacerbation' (diagnosis untagged!)
     → GOOD: 'this is a case of <SYMPTOM_VALUE>COPD exacerbation</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   BAD: 'any yellowing of your eyes or skin?' (body parts + symptom untagged)
     → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>yellowing</SYMPTOM_VALUE> of your <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>eyes</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> or <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>skin</SYMPTOM_LOCATION>?'
   BAD: 'she takes homeopathic drops <MEDICATION>for sleep</MEDICATION>' (tagged description, not med name)
     → GOOD: 'she takes <MEDICATION>homeopathic drops</MEDICATION> for sleep'
   BAD: 'I took something <MEDICATION>for pain</MEDICATION>' → GOOD: 'I took something for pain' (leave untagged if no drug name)
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>precautions</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' or '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>first baby</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — non-medical words are NEVER SYMPTOM_VALUE
   BAD: '<POLARITY>increasing</POLARITY>', '<POLARITY>worsening</POLARITY>', or '<POLARITY>likely</POLARITY>' — these are NOT polarity. Polarity is strictly yes/no/confirmed/absent.
   BAD: '<TEMPORAL>daily</TEMPORAL>' — 'daily' means HOW OFTEN (frequency), not WHEN. Use SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY or HABIT_FREQUENCY.
   BAD: '<HABIT_FREQUENCY>heavy</HABIT_FREQUENCY> smoker' — 'heavy' is intensity, not frequency. Leave untagged.
8. PRECISE BOUNDARIES — Tag the exact minimal span. Separate modifiers from the core entity
   (e.g. <SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>severe</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS> <SYMPTOM_VALUE>pain</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
   instead of wrapping them together).
   SPAN TRIMMING — Never include filler words inside a tag span:
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>like a pulling sensation</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>pulling sensation</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>'
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>it is feeling warm to touch</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>warm to touch</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>'
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>it is paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   Words like 'like a', 'it is', 'there is', 'I am having' must sit OUTSIDE the tag.
   TAG DISAMBIGUATION (avoid these common confusions):
   - SYMPTOM_VALUE = the symptom/condition NAME (fever, rash, diabetes).
     MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE = PAST condition or surgery mentioned as history.
     If the patient is CURRENTLY experiencing it → SYMPTOM_VALUE.
     If it happened IN THE PAST → MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE.
   - TEMPORAL = WHEN something happened (since two weeks, last month, 2024).
     SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY = HOW OFTEN it recurs (daily, on and off, every night).
     'daily' and 'every day' = SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY or HABIT_FREQUENCY, NEVER TEMPORAL.
   - HABIT_FREQUENCY = how much/often a HABIT occurs (2 packs a day, socially).
     SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY = how often a SYMPTOM recurs (twice a week, constantly).
   - MEDICAL_TEST_NAME = name of a test (HbA1c, X-ray, biopsy). Never tag a
     test name as MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE.

9. NATURAL FILLERS — sprinkle light spoken fillers (umm, ahh, uh) into some Patient turns, 0-1 per turn, never every turn. Fillers must sit OUTSIDE any tag span, never inside <TAG>...</TAG>.
10. LANGUAGE — ALL text MUST be in English. 'Indian English' means English
    sentences with Indian phrasing ('it is paining', 'sugar problem', 'gas trouble'),
    NOT Hindi/Hinglish sentences. Never output Hindi/Urdu words (mujhe, bahut, wala,
    ke paas, ho gaya, bilkul, gaon, chulha, beedi, gutka, pan masala, hookah,
    vaidya, churna, desi, haldi, ajwain). Use English equivalents instead
    (e.g., 'local healer' not 'vaidya', 'chewing tobacco' not 'gutka',
    'hand-rolled cigarette' not 'beedi'). Zero tolerance.
11. NO TAG-FREE ZONES — Never leave 2+ consecutive untagged turns.
    Closing summary/plan turns are especially rich in MEDICAL_TEST_NAME,
    MEDICATION, and SYMPTOM_VALUE — tag them all.
12. SPEAKERS — Only two speakers: 'Doctor' and 'Patient'. No third-party
    speakers (Family, Nurse, Junior, etc.). If a family member is present,
    the Patient speaks on their behalf. Do NOT address a 'Junior' or student
    in the dialogue — only Doctor ↔ Patient interaction.

Return ONLY a valid JSON array. No preamble, no markdown fences.
[{"speaker": "Doctor"|"Patient", "intent": "...from list...", "text": "...tagged utterance..."}]

Style: patient downplays symptoms; doctor probes patiently.
Required terms: SYMPTOM_VALUE: breathlessness, loose motion | TEMPORAL: since two weeks | SYMPTOM_LOCATION: chest | SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS: worse at night | SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY: every night | MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE: diabetes, hypertension | MEDICATION: metformin, inhaler | MEDICAL_TEST_NAME: chest X-ray, HbA1c | HABIT_VALUE: smoking | HABIT_FREQUENCY: half a pack a day | EXPOSURE_VALUE: dust | POLARITY: yes, no

Assistant:
[
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Basic_Information", "text": "Good morning. What has been bothering you?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Symptom", "text": "Doctor, <TEMPORAL>since two weeks</TEMPORAL> I am having <SYMPTOM_VALUE>breathlessness</SYMPTOM_VALUE>. It is <SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>worse at night</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS> and happening <SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY>every night</SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY>."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Symptom", "text": "Any <SYMPTOM_VALUE>loose motion</SYMPTOM_VALUE> or <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>stomach</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> problem also?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Symptom", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY> doctor, on and off. My <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>chest</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> feels heavy when lying down."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Any history of <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>diabetes</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE> or <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>hypertension</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY>, both are there doctor. I am on <MEDICATION>metformin</MEDICATION> for sugar and using <MEDICATION>inhaler</MEDICATION> when needed."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Are you still <HABIT_VALUE>smoking</HABIT_VALUE>?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY> doctor, <HABIT_FREQUENCY>half a pack a day</HABIT_FREQUENCY>. I know I should quit."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Any <EXPOSURE_VALUE>dust</EXPOSURE_VALUE> or fume exposure at work?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>No</POLARITY> doctor, I am retired now."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Inform-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment", "text": "Alright. We will do a <MEDICAL_TEST_NAME>chest X-ray</MEDICAL_TEST_NAME> and <MEDICAL_TEST_NAME>HbA1c</MEDICAL_TEST_NAME> today. The smoking history combined with your age is a concern."}
]

Your output trains Named Entity Recognition (NER) models — quality and entity density are paramount.

━━━ OUTPUT FORMAT ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Inline XML entity tags wrapping every span, embedded in natural speech:
  <SYMPTOM_VALUE>chest pain</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
  <TEMPORAL>since last week</TEMPORAL>
ALLOWED TAGS — exactly these 12, never invent others:
  POLARITY | SYMPTOM_VALUE | TEMPORAL | MEDICATION | EXPOSURE_VALUE
  SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS | MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE | SYMPTOM_LOCATION
  MEDICAL_TEST_NAME | HABIT_VALUE | HABIT_FREQUENCY | SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY
TAG CASING: ALL tag names MUST be FULLY UPPERCASE. Write <SYMPTOM_VALUE>
  not <SYMPTOM_Value> or <Symptom_Value>. Every letter after '<' must be uppercase or underscore.
NESTING: forbidden. Each token belongs to exactly one tag or is O.

━━━ INTENT CLASSIFICATION ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
For EVERY turn, you must classify the speaker's primary intent.
ALLOWED INTENTS (Select exactly one per turn from this list):
  Request-Etiology | Request-Precautions | Request-Medical_Advice
  Inform-Etiology | Diagnose | Request-Basic_Information
  Request-Drug_Recommendation | Inform-Medical_Advice
  Request-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment | Inform-Basic_Information
  Inform-Precautions | Inform-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment
  Inform-Drug_Recommendation | Request-Symptom | Inform-Symptom | Other

INTENT DISAMBIGUATION (use these definitions to choose correctly):
  Diagnose = doctor NAMES or IDENTIFIES the condition/disease.
  Inform-Medical_Advice = doctor explains treatment PLAN or clinical reasoning.
  Inform-Precautions = doctor warns about RISKS, side effects, things to AVOID.
  Inform-Drug_Recommendation = doctor prescribes or names SPECIFIC medicines.
    This is NOT the same as Inform-Medical_Advice. Use Inform-Drug_Recommendation
    when the doctor says 'I am prescribing X', 'take Y tablet', 'start Z syrup'.
  Other = ONLY greetings, farewells, or personal chat with ZERO medical content.
    'What brings you here today?' or 'What problem?' = Request-Basic_Information, NOT Other.
    These turns may have zero NER tags — but ONLY these turns.

━━━ QUALITY RULES ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1. MEDICAL PLAUSIBILITY — one coherent clinical scenario throughout.
   Never list terms mechanically. Each term must arise from the narrative.
2. INDIAN ENGLISH AUTHENTICITY — use colloquialisms organically:
   'sugar problem', 'gastric issue', 'BP shooting up', 'loose motion',
   'stone problem', 'urine problem', 'pain-killers only', 'it is paining'.
3. ENTITY DENSITY — every utterance from BOTH Doctor AND Patient past
   the opening greeting must carry ≥1 tagged entity. When the doctor
   mentions a symptom, test, or medication by name, tag it even in
   questions or summaries (e.g., 'Is there any <SYMPTOM_VALUE>swelling</SYMPTOM_VALUE>?').
   Target 40–50 total spans per dialogue.
   Minimum: 2 tags per turn average across the full dialogue.
   ZERO-TAG TURNS: Turns with zero tags are acceptable when the text
   genuinely contains no medical terms (e.g., 'What is bothering you?').
   But if a SPECIFIC medical term IS present, it MUST be tagged —
   never skip a relevant entity just because the turn is conversational.
   BAD: 'Do you smoke or drink?' (untagged) → GOOD: 'Do you <HABIT_VALUE>smoke</HABIT_VALUE> or <HABIT_VALUE>drink</HABIT_VALUE>?'
   BAD: 'Doctor, anemia — I do not know what that means' (untagged) → tag <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>anemia</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>
   OVER-TAGGING WARNING: Do NOT tag generic/vague words as medical entities:
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>health</SYMPTOM_VALUE>', '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>problem</SYMPTOM_VALUE>',
     '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>issue</SYMPTOM_VALUE>', '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>condition</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — these are too vague.
   Only tag SPECIFIC clinical terms (fever, anemia, paining, bleeding, diabetes, rash, etc.).
4. POLARITY BALANCE — mix affirmative ('yes doctor', 'confirmed', 'active')
   with negative ('no', 'not at all', 'stopped', 'denied', 'never').
   POLARITY is ONLY for binary yes/no confirmation/denial. NEVER tag
   trend words (increasing, worsening), certainty (likely, possibly), or
   state descriptors (uncontrolled, detected) as POLARITY.
5. LENGTH — 25 utterances total (Doctor + Patient combined).
6. STYLE — follow the per-request style instruction faithfully.
7. NO INVENTED TAG NAMES — use only the 12 allowed tags listed above.
   Do not invent new tag names. However, you MUST tag every medical
   entity that naturally appears in the dialogue, even if it was not
   in the 'Required terms' list. Required terms are minimum guarantees,
   not limits.
   CRITICAL: You must aggressively tag EVERY single mention of a body
   part (e.g., stomach, jaw, leg, ankle, head, bottom, belly, eyes, skin,
   knee, chest, wrist, temple, groin, prostate) as <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>.
   Never leave a medical term, body part, or symptom untagged, even if:
   - it is repeated (tag EVERY mention, not just the first)
   - it appears in a doctor's question or summary
   - the patient uses shy/indirect/colloquial language
   - it is a negated entity ('no <SYMPTOM_VALUE>fever</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — still tag it)
   - it is a diagnosis term in a Diagnose turn (tag the condition name!)
   - it uses Indian English verb forms: 'paining' = <SYMPTOM_VALUE>paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
   - it refers to a condition by name: 'anemia' = <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>anemia</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>
   - it is negated with 'nothing like': 'nothing like <SYMPTOM_VALUE>bleeding</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   NEGATIVE EXAMPLES (DO NOT DO THIS):
   BAD: 'any problem near your bottom?' → GOOD: 'near your <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>bottom</SYMPTOM_LOCATION>?'
   BAD: 'is there any swelling or lump?' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>swelling</SYMPTOM_VALUE> or <SYMPTOM_VALUE>lump</SYMPTOM_VALUE>?'
   BAD: 'constipation... straining... motion is hard' (all untagged)
     → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>constipation</SYMPTOM_VALUE>... <SYMPTOM_VALUE>straining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   BAD: 'this is a case of COPD exacerbation' (diagnosis untagged!)
     → GOOD: 'this is a case of <SYMPTOM_VALUE>COPD exacerbation</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   BAD: 'any yellowing of your eyes or skin?' (body parts + symptom untagged)
     → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>yellowing</SYMPTOM_VALUE> of your <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>eyes</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> or <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>skin</SYMPTOM_LOCATION>?'
   BAD: 'she takes homeopathic drops <MEDICATION>for sleep</MEDICATION>' (tagged description, not med name)
     → GOOD: 'she takes <MEDICATION>homeopathic drops</MEDICATION> for sleep'
   BAD: 'I took something <MEDICATION>for pain</MEDICATION>' → GOOD: 'I took something for pain' (leave untagged if no drug name)
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>precautions</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' or '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>first baby</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — non-medical words are NEVER SYMPTOM_VALUE
   BAD: '<POLARITY>increasing</POLARITY>', '<POLARITY>worsening</POLARITY>', or '<POLARITY>likely</POLARITY>' — these are NOT polarity. Polarity is strictly yes/no/confirmed/absent.
   BAD: '<TEMPORAL>daily</TEMPORAL>' — 'daily' means HOW OFTEN (frequency), not WHEN. Use SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY or HABIT_FREQUENCY.
   BAD: '<HABIT_FREQUENCY>heavy</HABIT_FREQUENCY> smoker' — 'heavy' is intensity, not frequency. Leave untagged.
8. PRECISE BOUNDARIES — Tag the exact minimal span. Separate modifiers from the core entity
   (e.g. <SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>severe</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS> <SYMPTOM_VALUE>pain</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
   instead of wrapping them together).
   SPAN TRIMMING — Never include filler words inside a tag span:
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>like a pulling sensation</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>pulling sensation</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>'
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>it is feeling warm to touch</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>warm to touch</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>'
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>it is paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   Words like 'like a', 'it is', 'there is', 'I am having' must sit OUTSIDE the tag.
   TAG DISAMBIGUATION (avoid these common confusions):
   - SYMPTOM_VALUE = the symptom/condition NAME (fever, rash, diabetes).
     MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE = PAST condition or surgery mentioned as history.
     If the patient is CURRENTLY experiencing it → SYMPTOM_VALUE.
     If it happened IN THE PAST → MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE.
   - TEMPORAL = WHEN something happened (since two weeks, last month, 2024).
     SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY = HOW OFTEN it recurs (daily, on and off, every night).
     'daily' and 'every day' = SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY or HABIT_FREQUENCY, NEVER TEMPORAL.
   - HABIT_FREQUENCY = how much/often a HABIT occurs (2 packs a day, socially).
     SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY = how often a SYMPTOM recurs (twice a week, constantly).
   - MEDICAL_TEST_NAME = name of a test (HbA1c, X-ray, biopsy). Never tag a
     test name as MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE.

9. NATURAL FILLERS — sprinkle light spoken fillers (umm, ahh, uh) into some Patient turns, 0-1 per turn, never every turn. Fillers must sit OUTSIDE any tag span, never inside <TAG>...</TAG>.
10. LANGUAGE — ALL text MUST be in English. 'Indian English' means English
    sentences with Indian phrasing ('it is paining', 'sugar problem', 'gas trouble'),
    NOT Hindi/Hinglish sentences. Never output Hindi/Urdu words (mujhe, bahut, wala,
    ke paas, ho gaya, bilkul, gaon, chulha, beedi, gutka, pan masala, hookah,
    vaidya, churna, desi, haldi, ajwain). Use English equivalents instead
    (e.g., 'local healer' not 'vaidya', 'chewing tobacco' not 'gutka',
    'hand-rolled cigarette' not 'beedi'). Zero tolerance.
11. NO TAG-FREE ZONES — Never leave 2+ consecutive untagged turns.
    Closing summary/plan turns are especially rich in MEDICAL_TEST_NAME,
    MEDICATION, and SYMPTOM_VALUE — tag them all.
12. SPEAKERS — Only two speakers: 'Doctor' and 'Patient'. No third-party
    speakers (Family, Nurse, Junior, etc.). If a family member is present,
    the Patient speaks on their behalf. Do NOT address a 'Junior' or student
    in the dialogue — only Doctor ↔ Patient interaction.

Return ONLY a valid JSON array. No preamble, no markdown fences.
[{"speaker": "Doctor"|"Patient", "intent": "...from list...", "text": "...tagged utterance..."}]

━━━ ONE-SHOT EXAMPLE (all 12 tags) ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Style: patient downplays symptoms; doctor probes patiently.
Required terms: SYMPTOM_VALUE: breathlessness, loose motion | TEMPORAL: since two weeks | SYMPTOM_LOCATION: chest | SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS: worse at night | SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY: every night | MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE: diabetes, hypertension | MEDICATION: metformin, inhaler | MEDICAL_TEST_NAME: chest X-ray, HbA1c | HABIT_VALUE: smoking | HABIT_FREQUENCY: half a pack a day | EXPOSURE_VALUE: dust | POLARITY: yes, no

Assistant:
[
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Basic_Information", "text": "Good morning. What has been bothering you?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Symptom", "text": "Doctor, <TEMPORAL>since two weeks</TEMPORAL> I am having <SYMPTOM_VALUE>breathlessness</SYMPTOM_VALUE>. It is <SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>worse at night</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS> and happening <SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY>every night</SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY>."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Symptom", "text": "Any <SYMPTOM_VALUE>loose motion</SYMPTOM_VALUE> or <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>stomach</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> problem also?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Symptom", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY> doctor, on and off. My <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>chest</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> feels heavy when lying down."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Any history of <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>diabetes</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE> or <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>hypertension</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY>, both are there doctor. I am on <MEDICATION>metformin</MEDICATION> for sugar and using <MEDICATION>inhaler</MEDICATION> when needed."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Are you still <HABIT_VALUE>smoking</HABIT_VALUE>?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY> doctor, <HABIT_FREQUENCY>half a pack a day</HABIT_FREQUENCY>. I know I should quit."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Any <EXPOSURE_VALUE>dust</EXPOSURE_VALUE> or fume exposure at work?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>No</POLARITY> doctor, I am retired now."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Inform-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment", "text": "Alright. We will do a <MEDICAL_TEST_NAME>chest X-ray</MEDICAL_TEST_NAME> and <MEDICAL_TEST_NAME>HbA1c</MEDICAL_TEST_NAME> today. The smoking history combined with your age is a concern."}
]

Your output trains Named Entity Recognition (NER) models — quality and entity density are paramount.

━━━ OUTPUT FORMAT ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Inline XML entity tags wrapping every span, embedded in natural speech:
  <SYMPTOM_VALUE>chest pain</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
  <TEMPORAL>since last week</TEMPORAL>
ALLOWED TAGS — exactly these 12, never invent others:
  POLARITY | SYMPTOM_VALUE | TEMPORAL | MEDICATION | EXPOSURE_VALUE
  SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS | MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE | SYMPTOM_LOCATION
  MEDICAL_TEST_NAME | HABIT_VALUE | HABIT_FREQUENCY | SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY
TAG CASING: ALL tag names MUST be FULLY UPPERCASE. Write <SYMPTOM_VALUE>
  not <SYMPTOM_Value> or <Symptom_Value>. Every letter after '<' must be uppercase or underscore.
NESTING: forbidden. Each token belongs to exactly one tag or is O.

━━━ INTENT CLASSIFICATION ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
For EVERY turn, you must classify the speaker's primary intent.
ALLOWED INTENTS (Select exactly one per turn from this list):
  Request-Etiology | Request-Precautions | Request-Medical_Advice
  Inform-Etiology | Diagnose | Request-Basic_Information
  Request-Drug_Recommendation | Inform-Medical_Advice
  Request-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment | Inform-Basic_Information
  Inform-Precautions | Inform-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment
  Inform-Drug_Recommendation | Request-Symptom | Inform-Symptom | Other

INTENT DISAMBIGUATION (use these definitions to choose correctly):
  Diagnose = doctor NAMES or IDENTIFIES the condition/disease.
  Inform-Medical_Advice = doctor explains treatment PLAN or clinical reasoning.
  Inform-Precautions = doctor warns about RISKS, side effects, things to AVOID.
  Inform-Drug_Recommendation = doctor prescribes or names SPECIFIC medicines.
    This is NOT the same as Inform-Medical_Advice. Use Inform-Drug_Recommendation
    when the doctor says 'I am prescribing X', 'take Y tablet', 'start Z syrup'.
  Other = ONLY greetings, farewells, or personal chat with ZERO medical content.
    'What brings you here today?' or 'What problem?' = Request-Basic_Information, NOT Other.
    These turns may have zero NER tags — but ONLY these turns.

━━━ QUALITY RULES ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1. MEDICAL PLAUSIBILITY — one coherent clinical scenario throughout.
   Never list terms mechanically. Each term must arise from the narrative.
2. INDIAN ENGLISH AUTHENTICITY — use colloquialisms organically:
   'sugar problem', 'gastric issue', 'BP shooting up', 'loose motion',
   'stone problem', 'urine problem', 'pain-killers only', 'it is paining'.
3. ENTITY DENSITY — every utterance from BOTH Doctor AND Patient past
   the opening greeting must carry ≥1 tagged entity. When the doctor
   mentions a symptom, test, or medication by name, tag it even in
   questions or summaries (e.g., 'Is there any <SYMPTOM_VALUE>swelling</SYMPTOM_VALUE>?').
   Target 40–50 total spans per dialogue.
   Minimum: 2 tags per turn average across the full dialogue.
   ZERO-TAG TURNS: Turns with zero tags are acceptable when the text
   genuinely contains no medical terms (e.g., 'What is bothering you?').
   But if a SPECIFIC medical term IS present, it MUST be tagged —
   never skip a relevant entity just because the turn is conversational.
   BAD: 'Do you smoke or drink?' (untagged) → GOOD: 'Do you <HABIT_VALUE>smoke</HABIT_VALUE> or <HABIT_VALUE>drink</HABIT_VALUE>?'
   BAD: 'Doctor, anemia — I do not know what that means' (untagged) → tag <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>anemia</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>
   OVER-TAGGING WARNING: Do NOT tag generic/vague words as medical entities:
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>health</SYMPTOM_VALUE>', '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>problem</SYMPTOM_VALUE>',
     '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>issue</SYMPTOM_VALUE>', '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>condition</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — these are too vague.
   Only tag SPECIFIC clinical terms (fever, anemia, paining, bleeding, diabetes, rash, etc.).
4. POLARITY BALANCE — mix affirmative ('yes doctor', 'confirmed', 'active')
   with negative ('no', 'not at all', 'stopped', 'denied', 'never').
   POLARITY is ONLY for binary yes/no confirmation/denial. NEVER tag
   trend words (increasing, worsening), certainty (likely, possibly), or
   state descriptors (uncontrolled, detected) as POLARITY.
5. LENGTH — 25 utterances total (Doctor + Patient combined).
6. STYLE — follow the per-request style instruction faithfully.
7. NO INVENTED TAG NAMES — use only the 12 allowed tags listed above.
   Do not invent new tag names. However, you MUST tag every medical
   entity that naturally appears in the dialogue, even if it was not
   in the 'Required terms' list. Required terms are minimum guarantees,
   not limits.
   CRITICAL: You must aggressively tag EVERY single mention of a body
   part (e.g., stomach, jaw, leg, ankle, head, bottom, belly, eyes, skin,
   knee, chest, wrist, temple, groin, prostate) as <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>.
   Never leave a medical term, body part, or symptom untagged, even if:
   - it is repeated (tag EVERY mention, not just the first)
   - it appears in a doctor's question or summary
   - the patient uses shy/indirect/colloquial language
   - it is a negated entity ('no <SYMPTOM_VALUE>fever</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — still tag it)
   - it is a diagnosis term in a Diagnose turn (tag the condition name!)
   - it uses Indian English verb forms: 'paining' = <SYMPTOM_VALUE>paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
   - it refers to a condition by name: 'anemia' = <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>anemia</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>
   - it is negated with 'nothing like': 'nothing like <SYMPTOM_VALUE>bleeding</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   NEGATIVE EXAMPLES (DO NOT DO THIS):
   BAD: 'any problem near your bottom?' → GOOD: 'near your <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>bottom</SYMPTOM_LOCATION>?'
   BAD: 'is there any swelling or lump?' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>swelling</SYMPTOM_VALUE> or <SYMPTOM_VALUE>lump</SYMPTOM_VALUE>?'
   BAD: 'constipation... straining... motion is hard' (all untagged)
     → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>constipation</SYMPTOM_VALUE>... <SYMPTOM_VALUE>straining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   BAD: 'this is a case of COPD exacerbation' (diagnosis untagged!)
     → GOOD: 'this is a case of <SYMPTOM_VALUE>COPD exacerbation</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   BAD: 'any yellowing of your eyes or skin?' (body parts + symptom untagged)
     → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>yellowing</SYMPTOM_VALUE> of your <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>eyes</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> or <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>skin</SYMPTOM_LOCATION>?'
   BAD: 'she takes homeopathic drops <MEDICATION>for sleep</MEDICATION>' (tagged description, not med name)
     → GOOD: 'she takes <MEDICATION>homeopathic drops</MEDICATION> for sleep'
   BAD: 'I took something <MEDICATION>for pain</MEDICATION>' → GOOD: 'I took something for pain' (leave untagged if no drug name)
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>precautions</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' or '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>first baby</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — non-medical words are NEVER SYMPTOM_VALUE
   BAD: '<POLARITY>increasing</POLARITY>', '<POLARITY>worsening</POLARITY>', or '<POLARITY>likely</POLARITY>' — these are NOT polarity. Polarity is strictly yes/no/confirmed/absent.
   BAD: '<TEMPORAL>daily</TEMPORAL>' — 'daily' means HOW OFTEN (frequency), not WHEN. Use SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY or HABIT_FREQUENCY.
   BAD: '<HABIT_FREQUENCY>heavy</HABIT_FREQUENCY> smoker' — 'heavy' is intensity, not frequency. Leave untagged.
8. PRECISE BOUNDARIES — Tag the exact minimal span. Separate modifiers from the core entity
   (e.g. <SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>severe</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS> <SYMPTOM_VALUE>pain</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
   instead of wrapping them together).
   SPAN TRIMMING — Never include filler words inside a tag span:
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>like a pulling sensation</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>pulling sensation</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>'
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>it is feeling warm to touch</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>warm to touch</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>'
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>it is paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   Words like 'like a', 'it is', 'there is', 'I am having' must sit OUTSIDE the tag.
   TAG DISAMBIGUATION (avoid these common confusions):
   - SYMPTOM_VALUE = the symptom/condition NAME (fever, rash, diabetes).
     MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE = PAST condition or surgery mentioned as history.
     If the patient is CURRENTLY experiencing it → SYMPTOM_VALUE.
     If it happened IN THE PAST → MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE.
   - TEMPORAL = WHEN something happened (since two weeks, last month, 2024).
     SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY = HOW OFTEN it recurs (daily, on and off, every night).
     'daily' and 'every day' = SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY or HABIT_FREQUENCY, NEVER TEMPORAL.
   - HABIT_FREQUENCY = how much/often a HABIT occurs (2 packs a day, socially).
     SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY = how often a SYMPTOM recurs (twice a week, constantly).
   - MEDICAL_TEST_NAME = name of a test (HbA1c, X-ray, biopsy). Never tag a
     test name as MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE.

9. NATURAL FILLERS — sprinkle light spoken fillers (umm, ahh, uh) into some Patient turns, 0-1 per turn, never every turn. Fillers must sit OUTSIDE any tag span, never inside <TAG>...</TAG>.
10. LANGUAGE — ALL text MUST be in English. 'Indian English' means English
    sentences with Indian phrasing ('it is paining', 'sugar problem', 'gas trouble'),
    NOT Hindi/Hinglish sentences. Never output Hindi/Urdu words (mujhe, bahut, wala,
    ke paas, ho gaya, bilkul, gaon, chulha, beedi, gutka, pan masala, hookah,
    vaidya, churna, desi, haldi, ajwain). Use English equivalents instead
    (e.g., 'local healer' not 'vaidya', 'chewing tobacco' not 'gutka',
    'hand-rolled cigarette' not 'beedi'). Zero tolerance.
11. NO TAG-FREE ZONES — Never leave 2+ consecutive untagged turns.
    Closing summary/plan turns are especially rich in MEDICAL_TEST_NAME,
    MEDICATION, and SYMPTOM_VALUE — tag them all.
12. SPEAKERS — Only two speakers: 'Doctor' and 'Patient'. No third-party
    speakers (Family, Nurse, Junior, etc.). If a family member is present,
    the Patient speaks on their behalf. Do NOT address a 'Junior' or student
    in the dialogue — only Doctor ↔ Patient interaction.

Return ONLY a valid JSON array. No preamble, no markdown fences.
[{"speaker": "Doctor"|"Patient", "intent": "...from list...", "text": "...tagged utterance..."}]

Style: patient downplays symptoms; doctor probes patiently.
Required terms: SYMPTOM_VALUE: breathlessness, loose motion | TEMPORAL: since two weeks | SYMPTOM_LOCATION: chest | SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS: worse at night | SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY: every night | MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE: diabetes, hypertension | MEDICATION: metformin, inhaler | MEDICAL_TEST_NAME: chest X-ray, HbA1c | HABIT_VALUE: smoking | HABIT_FREQUENCY: half a pack a day | EXPOSURE_VALUE: dust | POLARITY: yes, no

Assistant:
[
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Basic_Information", "text": "Good morning. What has been bothering you?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Symptom", "text": "Doctor, <TEMPORAL>since two weeks</TEMPORAL> I am having <SYMPTOM_VALUE>breathlessness</SYMPTOM_VALUE>. It is <SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>worse at night</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS> and happening <SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY>every night</SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY>."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Symptom", "text": "Any <SYMPTOM_VALUE>loose motion</SYMPTOM_VALUE> or <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>stomach</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> problem also?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Symptom", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY> doctor, on and off. My <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>chest</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> feels heavy when lying down."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Any history of <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>diabetes</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE> or <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>hypertension</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY>, both are there doctor. I am on <MEDICATION>metformin</MEDICATION> for sugar and using <MEDICATION>inhaler</MEDICATION> when needed."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Are you still <HABIT_VALUE>smoking</HABIT_VALUE>?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY> doctor, <HABIT_FREQUENCY>half a pack a day</HABIT_FREQUENCY>. I know I should quit."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Any <EXPOSURE_VALUE>dust</EXPOSURE_VALUE> or fume exposure at work?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>No</POLARITY> doctor, I am retired now."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Inform-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment", "text": "Alright. We will do a <MEDICAL_TEST_NAME>chest X-ray</MEDICAL_TEST_NAME> and <MEDICAL_TEST_NAME>HbA1c</MEDICAL_TEST_NAME> today. The smoking history combined with your age is a concern."}
]

Your output trains Named Entity Recognition (NER) models — quality and entity density are paramount.

━━━ OUTPUT FORMAT ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Inline XML entity tags wrapping every span, embedded in natural speech:
  <SYMPTOM_VALUE>chest pain</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
  <TEMPORAL>since last week</TEMPORAL>
ALLOWED TAGS — exactly these 12, never invent others:
  POLARITY | SYMPTOM_VALUE | TEMPORAL | MEDICATION | EXPOSURE_VALUE
  SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS | MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE | SYMPTOM_LOCATION
  MEDICAL_TEST_NAME | HABIT_VALUE | HABIT_FREQUENCY | SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY
TAG CASING: ALL tag names MUST be FULLY UPPERCASE. Write <SYMPTOM_VALUE>
  not <SYMPTOM_Value> or <Symptom_Value>. Every letter after '<' must be uppercase or underscore.
NESTING: forbidden. Each token belongs to exactly one tag or is O.

━━━ INTENT CLASSIFICATION ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
For EVERY turn, you must classify the speaker's primary intent.
ALLOWED INTENTS (Select exactly one per turn from this list):
  Request-Etiology | Request-Precautions | Request-Medical_Advice
  Inform-Etiology | Diagnose | Request-Basic_Information
  Request-Drug_Recommendation | Inform-Medical_Advice
  Request-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment | Inform-Basic_Information
  Inform-Precautions | Inform-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment
  Inform-Drug_Recommendation | Request-Symptom | Inform-Symptom | Other

INTENT DISAMBIGUATION (use these definitions to choose correctly):
  Diagnose = doctor NAMES or IDENTIFIES the condition/disease.
  Inform-Medical_Advice = doctor explains treatment PLAN or clinical reasoning.
  Inform-Precautions = doctor warns about RISKS, side effects, things to AVOID.
  Inform-Drug_Recommendation = doctor prescribes or names SPECIFIC medicines.
    This is NOT the same as Inform-Medical_Advice. Use Inform-Drug_Recommendation
    when the doctor says 'I am prescribing X', 'take Y tablet', 'start Z syrup'.
  Other = ONLY greetings, farewells, or personal chat with ZERO medical content.
    'What brings you here today?' or 'What problem?' = Request-Basic_Information, NOT Other.
    These turns may have zero NER tags — but ONLY these turns.

━━━ QUALITY RULES ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1. MEDICAL PLAUSIBILITY — one coherent clinical scenario throughout.
   Never list terms mechanically. Each term must arise from the narrative.
2. INDIAN ENGLISH AUTHENTICITY — use colloquialisms organically:
   'sugar problem', 'gastric issue', 'BP shooting up', 'loose motion',
   'stone problem', 'urine problem', 'pain-killers only', 'it is paining'.
3. ENTITY DENSITY — every utterance from BOTH Doctor AND Patient past
   the opening greeting must carry ≥1 tagged entity. When the doctor
   mentions a symptom, test, or medication by name, tag it even in
   questions or summaries (e.g., 'Is there any <SYMPTOM_VALUE>swelling</SYMPTOM_VALUE>?').
   Target 40–50 total spans per dialogue.
   Minimum: 2 tags per turn average across the full dialogue.
   ZERO-TAG TURNS: Turns with zero tags are acceptable when the text
   genuinely contains no medical terms (e.g., 'What is bothering you?').
   But if a SPECIFIC medical term IS present, it MUST be tagged —
   never skip a relevant entity just because the turn is conversational.
   BAD: 'Do you smoke or drink?' (untagged) → GOOD: 'Do you <HABIT_VALUE>smoke</HABIT_VALUE> or <HABIT_VALUE>drink</HABIT_VALUE>?'
   BAD: 'Doctor, anemia — I do not know what that means' (untagged) → tag <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>anemia</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>
   OVER-TAGGING WARNING: Do NOT tag generic/vague words as medical entities:
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>health</SYMPTOM_VALUE>', '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>problem</SYMPTOM_VALUE>',
     '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>issue</SYMPTOM_VALUE>', '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>condition</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — these are too vague.
   Only tag SPECIFIC clinical terms (fever, anemia, paining, bleeding, diabetes, rash, etc.).
4. POLARITY BALANCE — mix affirmative ('yes doctor', 'confirmed', 'active')
   with negative ('no', 'not at all', 'stopped', 'denied', 'never').
   POLARITY is ONLY for binary yes/no confirmation/denial. NEVER tag
   trend words (increasing, worsening), certainty (likely, possibly), or
   state descriptors (uncontrolled, detected) as POLARITY.
5. LENGTH — 25 utterances total (Doctor + Patient combined).
6. STYLE — follow the per-request style instruction faithfully.
7. NO INVENTED TAG NAMES — use only the 12 allowed tags listed above.
   Do not invent new tag names. However, you MUST tag every medical
   entity that naturally appears in the dialogue, even if it was not
   in the 'Required terms' list. Required terms are minimum guarantees,
   not limits.
   CRITICAL: You must aggressively tag EVERY single mention of a body
   part (e.g., stomach, jaw, leg, ankle, head, bottom, belly, eyes, skin,
   knee, chest, wrist, temple, groin, prostate) as <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>.
   Never leave a medical term, body part, or symptom untagged, even if:
   - it is repeated (tag EVERY mention, not just the first)
   - it appears in a doctor's question or summary
   - the patient uses shy/indirect/colloquial language
   - it is a negated entity ('no <SYMPTOM_VALUE>fever</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — still tag it)
   - it is a diagnosis term in a Diagnose turn (tag the condition name!)
   - it uses Indian English verb forms: 'paining' = <SYMPTOM_VALUE>paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
   - it refers to a condition by name: 'anemia' = <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>anemia</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>
   - it is negated with 'nothing like': 'nothing like <SYMPTOM_VALUE>bleeding</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   NEGATIVE EXAMPLES (DO NOT DO THIS):
   BAD: 'any problem near your bottom?' → GOOD: 'near your <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>bottom</SYMPTOM_LOCATION>?'
   BAD: 'is there any swelling or lump?' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>swelling</SYMPTOM_VALUE> or <SYMPTOM_VALUE>lump</SYMPTOM_VALUE>?'
   BAD: 'constipation... straining... motion is hard' (all untagged)
     → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>constipation</SYMPTOM_VALUE>... <SYMPTOM_VALUE>straining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   BAD: 'this is a case of COPD exacerbation' (diagnosis untagged!)
     → GOOD: 'this is a case of <SYMPTOM_VALUE>COPD exacerbation</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   BAD: 'any yellowing of your eyes or skin?' (body parts + symptom untagged)
     → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>yellowing</SYMPTOM_VALUE> of your <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>eyes</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> or <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>skin</SYMPTOM_LOCATION>?'
   BAD: 'she takes homeopathic drops <MEDICATION>for sleep</MEDICATION>' (tagged description, not med name)
     → GOOD: 'she takes <MEDICATION>homeopathic drops</MEDICATION> for sleep'
   BAD: 'I took something <MEDICATION>for pain</MEDICATION>' → GOOD: 'I took something for pain' (leave untagged if no drug name)
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>precautions</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' or '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>first baby</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' — non-medical words are NEVER SYMPTOM_VALUE
   BAD: '<POLARITY>increasing</POLARITY>', '<POLARITY>worsening</POLARITY>', or '<POLARITY>likely</POLARITY>' — these are NOT polarity. Polarity is strictly yes/no/confirmed/absent.
   BAD: '<TEMPORAL>daily</TEMPORAL>' — 'daily' means HOW OFTEN (frequency), not WHEN. Use SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY or HABIT_FREQUENCY.
   BAD: '<HABIT_FREQUENCY>heavy</HABIT_FREQUENCY> smoker' — 'heavy' is intensity, not frequency. Leave untagged.
8. PRECISE BOUNDARIES — Tag the exact minimal span. Separate modifiers from the core entity
   (e.g. <SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>severe</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS> <SYMPTOM_VALUE>pain</SYMPTOM_VALUE>
   instead of wrapping them together).
   SPAN TRIMMING — Never include filler words inside a tag span:
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>like a pulling sensation</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>pulling sensation</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>'
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>it is feeling warm to touch</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>warm to touch</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>'
   BAD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>it is paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>' → GOOD: '<SYMPTOM_VALUE>paining</SYMPTOM_VALUE>'
   Words like 'like a', 'it is', 'there is', 'I am having' must sit OUTSIDE the tag.
   TAG DISAMBIGUATION (avoid these common confusions):
   - SYMPTOM_VALUE = the symptom/condition NAME (fever, rash, diabetes).
     MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE = PAST condition or surgery mentioned as history.
     If the patient is CURRENTLY experiencing it → SYMPTOM_VALUE.
     If it happened IN THE PAST → MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE.
   - TEMPORAL = WHEN something happened (since two weeks, last month, 2024).
     SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY = HOW OFTEN it recurs (daily, on and off, every night).
     'daily' and 'every day' = SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY or HABIT_FREQUENCY, NEVER TEMPORAL.
   - HABIT_FREQUENCY = how much/often a HABIT occurs (2 packs a day, socially).
     SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY = how often a SYMPTOM recurs (twice a week, constantly).
   - MEDICAL_TEST_NAME = name of a test (HbA1c, X-ray, biopsy). Never tag a
     test name as MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE.

9. NATURAL FILLERS — sprinkle light spoken fillers (umm, ahh, uh) into some Patient turns, 0-1 per turn, never every turn. Fillers must sit OUTSIDE any tag span, never inside <TAG>...</TAG>.
10. LANGUAGE — ALL text MUST be in English. 'Indian English' means English
    sentences with Indian phrasing ('it is paining', 'sugar problem', 'gas trouble'),
    NOT Hindi/Hinglish sentences. Never output Hindi/Urdu words (mujhe, bahut, wala,
    ke paas, ho gaya, bilkul, gaon, chulha, beedi, gutka, pan masala, hookah,
    vaidya, churna, desi, haldi, ajwain). Use English equivalents instead
    (e.g., 'local healer' not 'vaidya', 'chewing tobacco' not 'gutka',
    'hand-rolled cigarette' not 'beedi'). Zero tolerance.
11. NO TAG-FREE ZONES — Never leave 2+ consecutive untagged turns.
    Closing summary/plan turns are especially rich in MEDICAL_TEST_NAME,
    MEDICATION, and SYMPTOM_VALUE — tag them all.
12. SPEAKERS — Only two speakers: 'Doctor' and 'Patient'. No third-party
    speakers (Family, Nurse, Junior, etc.). If a family member is present,
    the Patient speaks on their behalf. Do NOT address a 'Junior' or student
    in the dialogue — only Doctor ↔ Patient interaction.

Return ONLY a valid JSON array. No preamble, no markdown fences.
[{"speaker": "Doctor"|"Patient", "intent": "...from list...", "text": "...tagged utterance..."}]

Style: patient downplays symptoms; doctor probes patiently.
Required terms: SYMPTOM_VALUE: breathlessness, loose motion | TEMPORAL: since two weeks | SYMPTOM_LOCATION: chest | SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS: worse at night | SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY: every night | MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE: diabetes, hypertension | MEDICATION: metformin, inhaler | MEDICAL_TEST_NAME: chest X-ray, HbA1c | HABIT_VALUE: smoking | HABIT_FREQUENCY: half a pack a day | EXPOSURE_VALUE: dust | POLARITY: yes, no

Assistant:
[
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Basic_Information", "text": "Good morning. What has been bothering you?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Symptom", "text": "Doctor, <TEMPORAL>since two weeks</TEMPORAL> I am having <SYMPTOM_VALUE>breathlessness</SYMPTOM_VALUE>. It is <SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS>worse at night</SYMPTOM_CHARACTERISTICS> and happening <SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY>every night</SYMPTOM_FREQUENCY>."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Symptom", "text": "Any <SYMPTOM_VALUE>loose motion</SYMPTOM_VALUE> or <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>stomach</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> problem also?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Symptom", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY> doctor, on and off. My <SYMPTOM_LOCATION>chest</SYMPTOM_LOCATION> feels heavy when lying down."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Any history of <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>diabetes</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE> or <MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>hypertension</MEDICAL_HISTORY_VALUE>?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY>, both are there doctor. I am on <MEDICATION>metformin</MEDICATION> for sugar and using <MEDICATION>inhaler</MEDICATION> when needed."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Are you still <HABIT_VALUE>smoking</HABIT_VALUE>?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>Yes</POLARITY> doctor, <HABIT_FREQUENCY>half a pack a day</HABIT_FREQUENCY>. I know I should quit."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Request-Etiology", "text": "Any <EXPOSURE_VALUE>dust</EXPOSURE_VALUE> or fume exposure at work?"},
  {"speaker": "Patient", "intent": "Inform-Etiology", "text": "<POLARITY>No</POLARITY> doctor, I am retired now."},
  {"speaker": "Doctor", "intent": "Inform-Existing_Examination_and_Treatment", "text": "Alright. We will do a <MEDICAL_TEST_NAME>chest X-ray</MEDICAL_TEST_NAME> and <MEDICAL_TEST_NAME>HbA1c</MEDICAL_TEST_NAME> today. The smoking history combined with your age is a concern."}
]
